newsitem.title: CANADA: DiamondWorks says its Sierra Leone mine evacuated.
newsitem.headline: DiamondWorks says its Sierra Leone mine evacuated.

text.p: The military coup in Sierra Leone has prompted DiamondWorks Ltd. to evacuate its mining personnel and to help more than 60 other people to leave the country, the company said on Thursday.
DiamonWorks said in a statement the evacuation was considered temporary.
Chairman Eric Friedland said the company suspended its bulk diamond sampling operations in Sierra Leone "for the time being."

"We are in regular contact with the Koidu site and are encouraged by reports taht the area has remained calm throughout the post-coup period," Friedland said. "Relationships with the commanders of the local military contigent remain cordial."
The company said a security team "will remain at the Koidu mine to protect DiamondWorks' assets."
"The professional security service made our compound the safest location in the area during the past week, providing a shelter for expatriates," Friedland said.

DiamondWorks principal diamond mining and exploration projects are in Angola. It also has interests in a diamond exploration venture in Canada's Northwest Territories, in five gold and polymetallic exploraiton ventures in China and in various gold exploration properties in Venezuela.
